clauses.title: Owns
clauses.body: Shared design system: `packages/ui` component library, theme, and the `/ui-samples` demo.

clauses.title: @workspace/ui/components/*
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-01` — `@workspace/ui/components/*` — shadcn component set. Apps import from here, never fork.

clauses.title: @workspace/ui/lib/utils → cn()
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-02` — `@workspace/ui/lib/utils` → `cn()` — class merge helper.

clauses.title: @workspace/ui/globals.css
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-03` — `@workspace/ui/globals.css` — theme tokens (CSS vars), imported once in root layout. The palette is monochrome except two semantic colors: `--destructive` and `--success` (+ `--success-foreground`), both defined for light and dark and mapped in `@theme inline` (`--color-success`). `--success` is the on/enabled color — a switch in its checked state today; any later status badge, dot or toast uses this token rather than a literal green.

clauses.title: Root layout providers: ThemeProvider
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-04` — Root layout providers: `ThemeProvider` (next-themes), `TooltipProvider`, `Toaster` (sonner). (`apps/web/app/layout.tsx`)

clauses.title: Route /backflip/ui-samples
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-05` — Route `/backflip/ui-samples` — admin-only component gallery (auth-gated). Not a sidebar item: it is a reference, reached from the Docs guide's "UI samples" link and the ⌘K palette ("Pages" group), so a builder can name a component when describing a feature without the gallery competing with real destinations in the nav. Renders every component, `d` toggles dark mode. (`apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/ui-samples/page.tsx`)

clauses.title: Routes /getting-started
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-18` — Routes `/getting-started` (three-phase index: 01 Discover / 02 Set up / 03 Start building) + `/getting-started/intro` (discovery: what Backflip is, whom for) + **two droplet setup wizards**: `/getting-started/setup-on-digitalocean-droplet` (pm2 flavour) and `/getting-started/setup-on-digitalocean-droplet-docker-flavour` (Docker Postgres + Caddy) + `/getting-started/start-building` (copy-ready coding-agent prompts, prompts only) — all public + static. Both wizards are client-only: operator variables never leave the browser — kept in component state + `sessionStorage` (tab-scoped, per-guide namespace; no password is ever persisted), rendered into copyable `devops/` commands. Shared shell + chrome in `getting-started/_components/`; per-flavour command strings in each guide's `_components/setup-vars.ts`. Mirrors `L2-DEVOPS-01`, `L2-DEVOPS-02`, `L2-DEVOPS-06`; command strings must track those. (`apps/web/app/getting-started/…`)

clauses.title: Deployed version marker: monorepo root package.json version, inlined at build time
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-19` — Deployed version marker: monorepo root `package.json` `version`, inlined at build time (`apps/web/next.config.ts` → `env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION`) and rendered by `apps/web/app/_components/app-version.tsx` as `v<version>` in small low-contrast type. Mounted on the public footer and the admin Overview — both surfaces (`L1-ARCH-01`). Build-time value; no runtime override, so it names the build in the live slot.

clauses.title: Route /backflip/docs
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-20` — Route `/backflip/docs` — admin docs explorer (capability `dashboard`). Renders the repo's three-level docs (`/docs/constitution.md`, `/docs/contracts/*.md`, `/docs/notes/*.md`) as a domain-chip-filtered L1 | L2 | L3 cascade over a markdown reading pane. Selection filters bidirectionally (pick any level → the other two narrow to what cites it / what it cites); rows carry child counts + drift badges. Header "Docs" link points here (was the GitHub README; README link kept in-page); also a `⌘K` jump target. No sidebar entry. The reading pane and the drift overview share one slot, so the pane carries an **Overview** control back to the list. (`apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/docs/page.tsx`)

clauses.title: Docs search
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-35` — Docs search — one input filters all three cascade columns on ID, title, body and domain (`matchesQuery`, case-insensitive substring). Lives in the query string as `q`; the input is local with a 200 ms debounce so keystrokes do not enter session history. (`docs-explorer.tsx`, `docs-graph.ts`)

clauses.title: Cascade constraint disclosure
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-36` — Cascade constraint disclosure — each column header names the selections narrowing it (`constraintsOn`) and clicking one clears that hop; a **Trace** bar above the columns shows the current L1 › L2 › L3 chain with per-hop removal. Filtering is never silent. (`docs-explorer.tsx`)

clauses.title: Guide worked example
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-40` — Guide worked example — `exampleTrace(graph)` derives one complete L1 → L2 → L3 chain from the live index (the L1 with the most implementers, then its contract with the most notes, preferring a note heading that is not generic). Rendered as three labelled cards — why it exists / what it promises / how it is built — that load the whole trace into the cascade on click. Derived, never curated, so it cannot name a retired clause. (`docs-graph.ts`, `docs-guide.tsx`)

clauses.title: Docs orientation
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-37` — Docs orientation — a dismissible strip (per-browser, `localStorage["backflip.docs.orientation"]`, read through `useSyncExternalStore`) stating the three levels and the citation direction, plus a **Guide** landing tab: level cards with live counts, the cite-upward/conflict-order rule, verified entry-point clauses, and the domain map. The drift list moves to a **Health** tab. Guide is the default. Page order is content-first: header, orientation, reading/guide pane, then domain chips, trace bar and the three columns — what you read above, what you navigate with below. (`docs-guide.tsx`, `docs-explorer.tsx`)

clauses.title: Docs URL state
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-38` — Docs URL state — `domain`, `l1`, `l2`, `l3`, `clause`, `view`, `q` are the explorer's only state: back/forward work, a reload keeps position, and any view is linkable. Navigations `push`; search `replace`s. Requires a `Suspense` boundary around the explorer (`useSearchParams`). (`docs/page.tsx`, `docs-explorer.tsx`)

clauses.title: Clause trace placement
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-39` — Clause trace placement — implements-up, notes/contracts-down and `@spec` code refs render as horizontal rows directly under the clause title, not in a side rail, with the reading pane full width below. (`clause-detail.tsx`)

clauses.title: Admin chrome theming
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-25` — Admin chrome theming — the signed-in user's sidebar + header palette. The protected layout resolves it server-side and stamps `data-chrome-theme="<id>"` on the shell wrapper (`SidebarProvider`), so the themed chrome arrives with the server HTML and never flashes the default. CSS lives in `packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css`: per-theme blocks set `--sidebar-*` plus a `--chrome-header-*` family, and two scoped rules re-point the base tokens (`--foreground`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--accent`, …) inside `[data-slot="site-header"]` and `[data-slot="sidebar-inner"]` so existing children need no theme awareness. Page content is never tinted. (`apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/layout.tsx`, `_components/site-header.tsx`, `account/_components/appearance-section.tsx`)

clauses.title: getChromePreferences(userId) → { theme, headerThemed }, plus setChromeTheme / setChromeHeaderTh…
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-27` — `getChromePreferences(userId)` → `{ theme, headerThemed }`, plus `setChromeTheme` / `setChromeHeaderThemed` (`apps/web/app/_lib/theme/preferences.ts`) — server-only read/upsert over `user_preference` (`L2-DB-33`). A missing row means every default; nothing is seeded at signup.

clauses.title: Header opt-out
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-32` — Header opt-out — `user_preference.chromeHeaderThemed` (`L2-DB-33`), surfaced as the "Tint the header too" switch. Off → the layout stamps `data-chrome-header="plain"`, whose CSS block points the `--chrome-header-*` tokens back at the stock palette; the sidebar stays themed and the header follows plain light/dark. Server action `saveChromeHeaderThemed(enabled)` (`account/_actions.ts`), self-scoped, revalidates the `/backflip` layout.

clauses.title: Custom theme
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-33` — Custom theme — id `custom`, stored as two `#rrggbb` colors in `user_preference` (`chromeCustomSurface`, `chromeCustomAccent`, `L2-DB-33`). It has **no** stylesheet block: `customChromeVars(surface, accent)` builds the same variable set a theme block declares and the layout emits it inline on the shell wrapper. Ink, border and ring are derived from the two picks (near-white or near-black by WCAG luminance, mixed with the surface to keep its hue), so no pick can be unreadable. Server action `saveCustomChrome(surface, accent)` validates both colors. Honours `L2-UI-32`: with the header plain the `--chrome-header-*` variables are omitted from the inline set rather than overridden — inline style outranks the opt-out rule. Rendered as a two-column card beside Default. (`chrome-themes.ts`, `account/_components/appearance-section.tsx`)

clauses.title: Admin sidebar nav
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-42` — Admin sidebar nav (`app-sidebar.tsx`) carries the **working surfaces** only: **Platform** (Overview → `/backflip`, cap `dashboard`) and a bottom-pinned **Settings** (Integrations → `/backflip/settings`, cap `settings`, icon `RiLinksLine`). Administrative destinations — Members (`/backflip/users`, cap `users.view`, icon `RiGroupLine`) and Account (`/backflip/account`) — live in the `NavUser` dropdown instead, so the rail stays short and the identity chip owns "who is here and who else is". Capabilities are unchanged and still gate both the menu item and the route; the Members item is hidden for a role without `users.view` (teammate), which is why `NavUser` imports `can`.

clauses.title: Menu items in the NavUser dropdown carry cursor-pointer.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-43` — Menu items in the `NavUser` dropdown carry `cursor-pointer`. The shared `DropdownMenuItem` ships `cursor-default` (native-menu convention); the sidebar user chip reads as a web control, so its items point like the ⌘K palette's do. Applied at the call site, so other dropdowns keep the stock cursor.

clauses.title: Chrome gradient
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-44` — Chrome gradient — every named theme paints its sidebar as a shallow tonal ramp plus one corner glow instead of a flat surface: `radial-gradient(circle at 0% 0%, --grad-glow, transparent 45%)` over `linear-gradient(160deg, --grad-top 0%, --grad-surface 30%, --grad-bottom 60%)`. The stops finish at 60% because the ramp is sized to the **viewport** (`L2-UI-46`) while the chrome occupies only the first ~60% of its 1114px gradient line; at 55/100 the sidebar showed just the top half of every ramp, which was invisible on the light palettes (0.012 L). The recipe is declared **once** in `globals.css`, against a selector list covering the live sidebar, the mobile sheet, the tinted header and the `.chrome-gradient` class the account preview tiles use; a theme opts in by declaring the three stops in its block. `default` ramps too, from stops declared beside `--background` in `:root`/`.dark` since it is the one theme that follows light/dark. `bg-sidebar` remains underneath as the flat base, so an unset variable degrades to the previous look rather than to nothing.

clauses.title: The chrome is an L
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-46` — The chrome is an L — full-height sidebar, header strip to its right — and both paint slices of **one** ramp via `background-attachment: fixed`, which makes the viewport the positioning area. Per-element gradients would restart at the seam and read as two gradients meeting at a corner. The header joins only when tinted (`L2-UI-32`) and not glass (`L2-UI-45`); the mobile sheet stays box-local, having no header beside it. Each half declares only `--grad-surface`, its own side of the chrome — **the stops, glow included, are inherited from the theme block**, so both ramp between identical colours. Re-pointing `--grad-glow` per element is what broke this last: `var(--sidebar-accent)` drops the literal's alpha and steps the seam ~5% L on every light palette, where the accent is darker than the surface. Guarded by a pixel check in `e2e/admin-chrome.spec.ts`, one palette per tone.

clauses.title: Gradient stops are literal colors, never color-mix() over var().
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-47` — Gradient stops are **literal colors**, never `color-mix()` over `var()`. The production CSS minifier folds such a `color-mix()` down to its first color, which silently turned the built ramp into white → surface → black while dev looked correct. Named palettes therefore spell their stops out in `globals.css` and mirror them in `CHROME_THEMES[].swatch.grad` (locked in both directions by `chrome-themes.test.ts`); `custom` derives its stops with `color-mix()` because they ship as inline style, which no build step rewrites.

clauses.title: Glass header
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-45` — Glass header — opt-in, off by default, stored as `user_preference.chromeHeaderGlass` (`L2-DB-33`) and stamped as `data-chrome-glass="on"` on the shell wrapper. The header sticks to the top of the scroll container; the wash, a sheen and the blur move to a `::before` — Safari jitters with `backdrop-filter` on a `position: sticky` element, and on the header the filter's containing block would trap a non-portaled fixed descendant. The gradient image is dropped (an opaque image sits in front of the blur), via an explicit `:not([data-chrome-glass="on"])` on the gradient selector rather than a specificity race, so the ramp cannot continue across the whole strip. Instead the header **starts opaque and fades into the glass**: an `::after` paints the real ramp (same recipe, same viewport-fixed positioning — literally the sidebar's gradient continuing) under a horizontal mask that fades it out over ~340px, revealing the blurred `::before`. Seam continuity is then exact (measured +0.0% L dark, ≤1.0% light, from −1.2%/+4.3%). The mask goes on `::after`, never `::before`: a mask clips an element's `backdrop-filter` result along with its paint, so masking the blur layer punches raw unblurred page through the holes.

clauses.title: Glass filter chains are backdrop colour correction, keyed on tone × app mode.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-49` — Glass filter chains are **backdrop colour correction**, keyed on tone × app mode. The composite is `α·wash + (1−α)·filter(backdrop)`; a named palette's tone is fixed (`L2-UI-29`) while the canvas follows light/dark, so there are four cases. Same polarity (dark palette in dark mode, light in light, and any untinted header) needs only `brightness()`. Opposite polarity cannot use it — pulling a white canvas to 0.13 needs `brightness(0.14)`, which scales content variation by the same factor into a flat grey, and `contrast()` pivots on 0.5 and clips — so those use `grayscale(1) invert(…)`, the only op that moves the mean across without crushing variance: the page supplies luminance texture, the palette supplies hue. Alpha is 0.80 throughout (0.72 left blurred text ~0.10 L off and patchy; past ~0.85 modulation drops under 0.02 L and stops reading as glass), and each palette's wash pre-compensates chroma by ÷0.8 because a neutral backdrop dilutes it by exactly (1−α). Selected by `data-chrome-tone`, stamped by the layout from the catalog's `group` (and from luminance for `custom`) — never a hand-kept list of palette ids. `default` carries no tone and takes the stock chain. No `backdrop-filter` support, `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, or print → solid header colour, pinning kept.

clauses.title: Build-loop pitch
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-48` — Build-loop pitch — the product's shortest self-description, as a four-prompt transcript (`clone …` / `set up and run this project locally` / `create a user for me and give me the login URL` / `build feature <...>`) between the line "You have Docker and dev tools ready." and "That's how you start a project now." The prompt strings live once, in `apps/web/app/_components/build-loop.tsx`, and are exported so the copy cannot drift between surfaces. Mounted on **both** surfaces (`L1-ARCH-01`): the public homepage directly under the hero as `BuildLoop` (its own section, eyebrow + heading + card), and the admin Overview as `BuildLoopTranscript compact` inside a card above the info cards. `README.md` carries the same four lines as a fenced block under the tagline. Rendered as flat type on a card, never as a terminal mock — no window chrome, no traffic lights.

clauses.title: Chrome controls take --chrome-header-input, not the seam colour.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-50` — Chrome **controls** take `--chrome-header-input`, not the seam colour. `--chrome-header-border` is deliberately a hairline (≈0.045 L from its surface, `L2-UI-29`) so the sidebar↔header seam reads as one surface; the header subtree re-points `--border` *and* used to re-point `--input` to it, which left the ⌘K jump control outlined at ~1.05:1 against the header — invisible on the dark palettes. Each palette now declares a separate `--chrome-header-input` (~0.28 L from the surface on dark, ~0.26 below it on light, landing both tones near 2.3:1), the header subtree points `--input` at it, and `header-search.tsx` asks for `border-input`. Stock chrome takes `--stock-input`. Still under the 3:1 WCAG non-text threshold — a deliberate stop, since a control whose label is legible on its own does not carry the boundary alone.

clauses.title: Header type matches the sidebar: the breadcrumb trail and the Docs link are text-[13px], the sa…
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-51` — Header type matches the sidebar: the breadcrumb trail and the Docs link are `text-[13px]`, the same size `app-sidebar.tsx` gives its menu items, so the two halves of the chrome read as one navigation surface rather than two scales.

clauses.title: Server action saveChromeTheme(theme)
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-28` — Server action `saveChromeTheme(theme)` (`account/_actions.ts`) — self-scoped to the session user, refuses ids outside the catalog, revalidates the `/backflip` **layout** (not just the page) so the shell re-renders.

clauses.title: Chrome theme catalog
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-26` — Chrome theme catalog (`apps/web/app/_lib/theme/chrome-themes.ts`): `default` plus fixed palettes — dark `slate` | `graphite` | `pine` | `aubergine`, light `gold` | `sky-blue` | `sage` | `rose-gold`. Each entry carries `id`, `label`, `group`, swatch colors for the picker and the three gradient stops (`L2-UI-44`, `L2-UI-47`). Hover/active rows sit ~0.085 L from the surface on the dark palettes and ~0.075 L **below** it on the light ones — the earlier 0.04 was too faint to find, and the stock sidebar's 0.015 was the faintest of all. Ids are the single source of truth: every named id has a matching `[data-chrome-theme="<id>"]` block in `globals.css`, and every such block has a catalog entry (locked by `chrome-themes.test.ts`). Stored per user in `user_preference.chromeTheme` as free text; `resolveChromeTheme()` narrows anything unknown back to `default`. `custom` (`L2-UI-33`) is a valid id but deliberately absent from the catalog array — it has no fixed swatch and renders as its own card.

clauses.title: shadcn config
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-06` — shadcn config (`packages/ui/components.json`): style `base-mira`, baseColor `neutral`, RSC on, icons `remixicon`, css vars on.

clauses.title: Aliases: components/ui → @workspace/ui/components, utils → @workspace/ui/lib/utils.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-07` — Aliases: components/ui → `@workspace/ui/components`, utils → `@workspace/ui/lib/utils`.

clauses.title: Clause titles strip the concern kind-tag
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-41` — Clause titles strip the concern kind-tag (`_(iface)_`, `_(inv)_`, …) before deriving a title, so a concern-grouped contract lists real clause text rather than its tag. (`parse-docs.ts`)

clauses.title: Docs index built at build time, never at runtime: a server-only module parses /docs//*.md
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-21` — Docs index built at **build time**, never at runtime: a `server-only` module parses `/docs/**/*.md` (headings, `L[123]-<CAT>-<NN>` IDs, `Implements L1:` / `Depends on L2:` / inline `L2-…` cite edges) and greps `@spec` tags across `apps/*`, `packages/*`, `devops/*` into one serializable index. `yarn workspace web docs:index` writes `docs-index.generated.json`; the workspace `build` script runs it before `next build`. Rationale: the Docker runner ships only `.next/standalone`, so `/docs` is absent at runtime. Dev reads the working tree live.

clauses.title: One theme source: packages/ui.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-08` — One theme source: `packages/ui`. No per-app component copies.

clauses.title: Overlay components
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-09` — Overlay components (tooltip/toast) require their providers mounted in root layout.

clauses.title: Web app transpiles @workspace/ui
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-10` — Web app transpiles `@workspace/ui` (`next.config.ts transpilePackages`).

clauses.title: Button infers base-ui nativeButton from its render element: <button> → true, any other element …
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-14` — `Button` infers base-ui `nativeButton` from its `render` element: `<button>` → true, any other element → false. Explicit `nativeButton` overrides. Link-buttons (`render={<a/>}` / `render={<Link/>}`) need no extra prop.

clauses.title: Shell containers hosting page content are shrinkable
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-15` — Shell containers hosting page content are shrinkable (`min-w-0`), so page content never forces the shell wider than its slot.

clauses.title: Docs explorer is read-only.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-22` — Docs explorer is read-only. No doc editing or writing from the admin UI.

clauses.title: Named chrome themes are fixed palettes: they do not follow the light/dark toggle, so a platform…
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-29` — Named chrome themes are **fixed palettes**: they do not follow the light/dark toggle, so a platform keeps its identity in either mode. Only `default` follows the mode. Chroma is held ≤ 0.10 on the dark surfaces and ≤ 0.03 on the light ones — enough hue separation to identify a platform at a glance, never a saturated surface. Aubergine sits at the top of that range deliberately: below ~0.08 a plum reads as grey-violet rather than as a colour. Eight named palettes: four dark, four light. Chrome borders sit ≈0.045 L from their own surface: sidebar and header share one tint, so their seam is a hairline rather than a rule. One border color for the whole chrome — the sidebar's right edge and the header's bottom edge are the same value in every palette.

clauses.title: One stylesheet serves both surfaces
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-34` — One stylesheet serves both surfaces (`L2-UI-03`), so every chrome-theme rule gates itself on `[data-chrome-theme]` — an attribute stamped only by the admin shell. No admin chrome rule may apply to a public page, including rules keyed on a `data-slot` a public component could also use.

clauses.title: Chrome theming is per user and cosmetic only.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-30` — Chrome theming is per user and cosmetic only. It changes no capability, is never used to signal environment or permission state, and an unknown stored id degrades to `default` rather than an unstyled shell.

clauses.title: Drift badges are derived on read, never stored: orphan = ID no L3 note cites
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-23` — Drift badges are derived on read, never stored: `orphan` = ID no L3 note cites (L1: no L2 implements), `no code` = ID with zero `@spec` references, `needs confirm` = clause carrying the confirmation marker **outside inline code** (a doc quoting the marker while describing this rule is not drift), `broken ref` = cites an ID defined nowhere in `/docs`. The landing view lists every badge with its count and a one-line meaning, zeros included, so the pills on the rows are always legible.

clauses.title: Component used without required provider → runtime context error.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-11` — Component used without required provider → runtime context error. Mount provider in root layout.

clauses.title: /ui-samples renders all components without error; dark toggle works.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-12` — `/ui-samples` renders all components without error; dark toggle works.

clauses.title: Any app imports a component via @workspace/ui/components/* and it themes correctly.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-13` — Any app imports a component via `@workspace/ui/components/*` and it themes correctly.

clauses.title: No surface produces page-level horizontal scroll at ≥640px.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-16` — No surface produces page-level horizontal scroll at ≥640px.

clauses.title: Public + admin surfaces load with zero console errors/warnings.
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-17` — Public + admin surfaces load with zero console errors/warnings.

clauses.title: Every ID present in /docs appears in the explorer index; broken or unknown ID citations render …
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-24` — Every ID present in `/docs` appears in the explorer index; broken or unknown ID citations render as badges, never crash the page.

clauses.title: Picking a theme in /backflip/account → Appearance repaints the live sidebar + header at once, s…
clauses.body: - `L2-UI-31` — Picking a theme in `/backflip/account` → Appearance repaints the live sidebar + header at once, survives a reload and every navigation under `/backflip`, and is scoped to the picking user. A failed save rolls the shell back to the stored theme. Turning off "Tint the header too" leaves the sidebar themed and returns the header to plain light/dark, live and after reload; the tiles preview that state.

clauses.title: File map
clauses.body:
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/settings/page.tsx` — server; loads `ai_config`, maps to view model (no key decryption; `hasKey` boolean). Satisfies `L2-AI-01`.
- `settings/_components/ai-config-form.tsx` — one tab per supported provider (`L2-AI-04`), each carrying the per-provider fields (`L2-AI-05`). Client; Tabs per provider (provider selector), flat form content (no Card), inputs capped 320px. `useActionState(saveAiConfig)`. Fields: **default model** (`native-select`; per-provider default, individual AI features may request a different model at call time), API key (password, write-only), enabled + default provider (`Switch`, base-ui `name`). Static `MODELS` list per provider. (baseUrl/temperature columns exist but aren't in the form.) Page wraps each settings section in a `Card`. `ai-section.tsx` (client) toggles between a **summary** (per-provider status: default/enabled badges, model, masked key preview, or "Not configured" + "Edit settings" button) and the **edit** view (two-column: `AiConfigForm` left, vertical `Separator`, explanation prose right). Form takes `onSaved`/`onCancel`; on save success (`state.ok`) it returns to summary. Provider name shown as a title above the form.
- `settings/_lib/mask.ts` — server util: `keyPreview(apiKeyEnc)` decrypts (`L2-DB-16`) → `maskKey` (first 3 + last 4 around fixed 8-dot run; ≤8 chars fully masked). Preview computed in `page.tsx`; plaintext never sent to client. Satisfies `L2-AI-06`.
- `settings/_actions.ts` — `saveAiConfig` (`"use server"`): auth-gate → upsert on provider → encrypt key if provided → unset other defaults → `revalidatePath`. Satisfies `L2-AI-02`, `L2-AI-06..08`. Also `listAiModels(provider)`: auth-gate → read `ai_config` row → decrypt key server-side → `fetchProviderModels` → `{ok, models}` (or `ok:false` when no key / fetch fails — UI keeps fallback). Satisfies `L2-AI-13` (proposed).
- `settings/_lib/provider-models.ts` — server-only live model discovery (`@spec L2-AI-13`): anthropic `GET /v1/models` (x-api-key + anthropic-version, `after_id` pagination ≤5 pages), openai `GET /v1/models` (Bearer; filtered to chat families `gpt-*`/`o<N>`/`chatgpt-*`, non-chat variants excluded), google `GET v1beta/models` (x-goog-api-key, `generateContent`-capable only, `models/` prefix stripped, pageToken ≤5 pages). 10s timeout, provider error bodies never surfaced to the client.
- `settings/_hooks/use-provider-models.ts` — `useProviderModels(cfg)` (moved out of `ai-integration.tsx`; shared with the test modal). No key → empty list (no stale hardcoded fallback); key saved → static `MODELS` bridge, then live list via `listAiModels`; saved model always kept selectable.
- `ai-integration.tsx` model UI: no key → dropdown disabled ("Save an API key to load models…"), "Available models" panel hidden entirely. With key: dropdown disabled while loading; panel labels live vs fallback, scrolls past 72. Header carries a "Test integration" button (`RiFlaskLine`), disabled until some provider is enabled **and** has a key.
- `settings/_components/ai-test-dialog.tsx` — client; test modal (`@spec L2-AI-15`). Provider select (testable only, defaults to the default provider), model select (`useProviderModels`), prompt `Textarea` (4000 max, ⌘/Ctrl+↵ sends, `Kbd` hint). Submit → `fetch` the test route, read the body reader, append chunks to state → `Markdown`. States: idle / thinking (pulsing dots) / streaming (response box auto-scrolls) / error (generic message). Unmounted while closed, so a run never leaks into the next open; in-flight run aborted on unmount.
- `settings/_components/markdown.tsx` — client; `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm` with per-element Tailwind classes (no typography plugin in the design system). Raw HTML left disabled — model output is untrusted.
- `settings/_lib/ai-test.ts` — server-only call layer (`@spec L2-AI-14, L2-AI-16`): provider → `createAnthropic`/`createOpenAI`/`createGoogleGenerativeAI` with the decrypted key → `streamText`. **Awaits the first chunk before returning the stream**, so an up-front failure (bad key, unknown model) still becomes a 502 JSON body instead of a half-written response; a mid-stream failure keeps the partial and closes cleanly. System prompt asks for a short, well-structured markdown answer.
- `app/api/backflip/ai/test/route.ts` — `POST` (`@spec L2-AI-14, L2-AI-17..21`): auth + `settings` gate → per-user rate limit (`L2-AI-21`) → validate provider/model/prompt → read `ai_config` → require key + `enabled` → decrypt → stream `text/plain`, `no-store`. Node runtime. A route, not a server action, because the answer streams. Rate limit: `testRateLimiter` (shared `_lib/rate-limit.ts`, see [[auth]]), keyed on `session.user.id`, `TEST_MAX_PER_WINDOW` (20) per `TEST_WINDOW_MS` (5 min); over-limit → `429` + `Retry-After`. Bounds cost abuse of the org's stored provider key by an owner session (or a stolen owner cookie). In-process (single Node process per instance).
- `apps/web` dep `server-only` — guards `provider-models.ts` and `ai-test.ts` from client bundling.
- `apps/web` deps `ai` (7.x) + `@ai-sdk/anthropic`/`@ai-sdk/openai`/`@ai-sdk/google` (4.x) — `L1-STACK-11`; `zod` (AI SDK peer); `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`.
- `packages/db` — `ai_config` table + `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` (`L2-DB-16/17`). This is where the config lives and how the key is protected. Satisfies `L2-AI-03`.

clauses.section: Banner copy (why it reads the way it does)
clauses.title: Banner copy (why it reads the way it does)
clauses.body:
Default is a conversion problem, not a legal one — the consent gate is strict (`L2-ANALYTICS-06`), so *undecided* visitors are never measured either, and most people never click anything. Measured traffic ≈ accept rate.
- Old seed led with the cost ("We use cookies … via Google Analytics") and gave no reason to say yes.
- Current default asks for the visit, states the benefit, bounds the use ("we only ever look at totals, and never use it for ads"), then names Google Analytics + cookies. Same facts, cost last.
- Claims are about *our* use only. Don't add promises about what Google does with it — an operator can enable Google Signals/ads features and make them false.
- Layout stays symmetric: Decline and Accept, one click each, same bar. EDPB requires reject to be equally easy; it does not require identical styling, so primary Accept + outline Decline stays compliant. Never remove Decline, never bury it behind a second layer.
- Copy is operator-editable at `/backflip/settings`, so retuning needs no deploy. `FALLBACK_TEXT` in `analytics-gate.tsx` mirrors the seed and must be updated with it.

clauses.section: Why the config is fetched, not server-rendered
clauses.title: Why the config is fetched, not server-rendered
clauses.body:
Public pages (`/`, `/getting-started`, both guides) build as `○` static. Reading `analytics_config` in those pages — or in the root layout — would flip them to `ƒ`, and the root layout is shared with `/backflip`, so it would drag the whole app dynamic.

Chosen: **static pages + client fetch of `/api/public/analytics-config`.** The route is the only dynamic piece; the pages stay prerendered. Verified in the build route table (`L2-ANALYTICS-11`, `L2-ANALYTICS-20`).

Rejected alternatives:
- Server component wrapped in `cache()` inside the root layout — still forces a dynamic render, and pollutes the admin surface.
- Per-page async server component — would flip each public page to `ƒ`.
- Env var instead of DB config — loses the admin-editable banner copy, which is the point.

Cost of the choice: config changes reach visitors within ~5 min (cache window), and the banner appears one paint after hydration rather than in the prerendered HTML. Both acceptable for a consent bar.

clauses.title: Mount point
clauses.body: `AnalyticsGate` hangs off `SiteFooter` — the only chrome every public page renders and no admin page does (verified: `SiteFooter` is imported by exactly the 4 public pages). Structural enforcement of `L2-ANALYTICS-10`; no path sniffing at runtime. **If a public page is ever added without `SiteFooter`, analytics silently won't run there** — consider a public layout if the surface grows.

clauses.title: Gotchas hit
clauses.body:
- **Disabled textarea submits nothing.** First cut used `disabled={!bannerEnabled}` on the banner-text field; toggling the banner off and saving would have wiped the seeded copy (`FormData` omits disabled fields → `null`). Now `readOnly` + `aria-disabled` + `opacity-50`. See `L2-ANALYTICS-08`.
- **Measurement id is interpolated into a `<script src>`.** Public ≠ untrusted-safe: it's validated server-side against an allow-list charset and `encodeURIComponent`'d client-side.
- Route needs `force-dynamic`, else Next may try to evaluate it during `next build`, where no database is reachable.

- `yarn workspace web build` — passes. Route table unchanged for public pages: `○ /`, `○ /getting-started`, `○ /getting-started/setup-on-digitalocean-droplet`, `○ /getting-started/setup-on-digitalocean-droplet-docker-flavour`; new `ƒ /api/public/analytics-config`.

clauses.title: File map
clauses.body:
- `apps/web/app/_lib/auth/index.ts` — NextAuth(v5) config. Adapter `DrizzleAdapter(db)`, `session.strategy=jwt`. Providers conditional: Google when `isGoogleConfigured()`, Credentials when `isCredentialsEnabled()`. Callbacks: `signIn` (Google pre-registration + `profile.email_verified === true` gate, `L2-AUTH-41`; on success it writes `profile.picture` into `users.image` when it differs — `googlePicture()` accepts only a non-empty string — because email linking never touches the existing row, `L2-AUTH-45`); `jwt` stamps `tokenVersion` on sign-in (and, for Google, `token.picture` from the profile: the `user` it receives is the pre-sync row, so the session would otherwise show no avatar until the next login), and on later requests re-reads the user's `tokenVersion`/`role` from DB — mismatch/missing → `token.invalid`; `session` drops `user` when `invalid`. Credentials `authorize` normalizes the email (`.trim().toLowerCase()`, matches write paths) and throttles failed attempts per IP+email via `loginRateLimiter` (`L2-AUTH-40`): `blocked()` → generic `null`; `hit()` on failure; `reset()` on success. Exports `handlers, auth, signIn, signOut`. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-02`, `L2-AUTH-05`, `L2-AUTH-06` (JWT session strategy — no DB session rows), `L2-AUTH-09/10/11`, `L2-AUTH-33`, `L2-AUTH-36`, `L2-AUTH-40`, `L2-AUTH-41`, `L2-AUTH-45`.
- `apps/web/app/_lib/rate-limit.ts` — `createRateLimiter({max,windowMs,now?})` → `{blocked,hit,reset,retryAfterMs}`. In-process fixed-window counter (module-scoped Map); holds within ONE Node process only (matches the single-pm2/container-per-instance deployment) — a multi-instance setup would need a shared store. Injectable `now` for tests. Used by the login throttle (`L2-AUTH-40`) and the AI test endpoint (`L2-AI-22`, see [[ai]]).
- `apps/web/app/_lib/auth/config.ts` — server-only auth-mode flags: `isGoogleConfigured()` (both `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`+`AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET` set), `isCredentialsEnabled()` (`AUTH_CREDENTIALS_ENABLED=false` disables password login, but ONLY when Google is configured — fail-safe against lockout). Read in the Auth.js config, login page, and recovery actions; never a client component. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-33`.
- `apps/web/app/_lib/auth/types.ts` — module augmentation: `session.user.id`/`role` (`role` typed `Role`), JWT `id`/`role`.
- `apps/web/app/_lib/auth/permissions.ts` — pure/client-safe RBAC: `Role`, `ROLES`, `ROLE_LABELS`, `Capability`, capability map, `can()` + `canViewUsers`/`canEditUsers`/`canAccessSettings`. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-19`, `L2-AUTH-21`. Imported by server guards AND client UI (nav, edit gating) — keep it free of server-only imports.
- `apps/web/app/_lib/auth/guard.ts` — `requireCapability(cap)` server guard (`auth()` → redirect). Satisfies `L2-AUTH-20`, `L2-AUTH-22`.
- `apps/web/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` — `export { GET, POST } = handlers`; `runtime = "nodejs"`. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-03`.
- `apps/web/proxy.ts` — edge gate via `getToken` with `secureCookie` derived from `AUTH_URL` (behind a TLS-terminating proxy the edge request is plain http — protocol-inferred cookie name would miss `__Secure-authjs.session-token` and redirect-loop the login); `RECOVERY_PATHS` (forgot/reset-password) bypass the gate as public. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-01`, `L2-AUTH-08`, `L2-AUTH-12`.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(auth)/login/page.tsx` — login page (server; reads `from`, open-redirect guarded). Satisfies `L2-AUTH-04`.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(auth)/login/page.tsx` — `auth()` first: a valid session → `redirect("/backflip")` (moved off the edge, which can't check token version). Passes `credentialsEnabled`/`googleEnabled` (from `config.ts`) to the form.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(auth)/login/_components/login-form.tsx` — client form (`login-03` block). Renders by mode: both → Google button + separator + credentials form + "Forgot password?" link; Google-only (`!credentialsEnabled`) → Google button alone; credentials-only (`!googleEnabled`) → form alone. Credentials via `signIn("credentials", {redirect:false})`; Google via `signIn("google")`. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-33`.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/layout.tsx` — authed shell (server; `auth()` → user). SidebarProvider + AppSidebar + SidebarInset + header.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/_components/` — `app-sidebar` (nav items carry a `capability`, filtered by role via `can()`; Account item added), `nav-main`, `nav-secondary`, `site-header`, `nav-user` (Account item → `/backflip/account`; dropdown → `signOut`), `section-cards`, `dashboard-chart`, `recent-table`, `types` (`SessionUser.role: Role`).
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/page.tsx` — dashboard (capability `dashboard`, all roles). Aggregate stat cards + setup checklist shown to everyone; the **Recent members** card (names + emails) renders only when `canViewUsers(role)` (owner/admin), so a teammate never sees other members' emails. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-21/22`.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/users/page.tsx` — server; `requireCapability("users.view")`; reads users + derives login methods (`passwordHash` presence + `accounts` providers, hash never sent). Passes `sessionRole`/`sessionUserId`.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/users/_components/users-list.tsx` — stacked compact cards (avatar · name+email · role · login method, smaller font); Edit shown only when `canEditUsers`. Header carries an **Add user** button, rendered only when `canEditUsers` (owner).
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/users/_components/edit-user-dialog.tsx` — owner-only Dialog: name + email + role (`Select`); role field disabled when editing self (hidden field carries the unchanged role). Satisfies `L2-AUTH-22`, `L2-AUTH-23`.
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/users/_components/add-user-dialog.tsx` — owner-only Dialog: name + email + role (`Select`, default `teammate`) + optional password. Client `fetch("POST /api/backflip/users", JSON)`; on success surfaces the returned message via `sonner` toast (reports welcome-email status, incl. "not configured"), `router.refresh()` to reload the list, resets the form, closes. Non-2xx/`ok:false` → inline error. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-22`, `L2-AUTH-25`.
- `apps/web/app/_lib/validation.ts` — zod schemas for admin user management: `createUserSchema` / `updateUserSchema` (email format via `EMAIL_RE`, role via `isRole`, `PASSWORD_MIN`=8 on create) + `firstError()`. Rejects non-string JSON instead of coercing. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-42`.
- `apps/web/app/api/backflip/users/route.ts` — `POST` route handler (`runtime="nodejs"`): `users.edit` gate → `createUserSchema.safeParse(body)` (400 + first message on failure) → optional bcrypt password (blank → Google-only sign-in) → insert (unique-email 409) → best-effort `sendWelcomeEmail` (see [[email]]) → `revalidatePath` → JSON. Status: 201 · 400 · 401 · 403 · 409. Email failure/unconfigured never changes the 201. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-22`, `L2-AUTH-25`, `L2-AUTH-42`. (Aligns admin mutation with `L1-ARCH-03` API-endpoint model, unlike the server-action pattern used elsewhere.)
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/users/_actions.ts` — `updateUser` (`users.edit` gate, `updateUserSchema` validation, self-role guard; runs in a `db.transaction`: locks the target row + owner set `FOR UPDATE`, refuses demoting the last owner, bumps `tokenVersion` when email/role changes → revokes the target's sessions; unique-email pg 23505) + `deleteUser(userId)` (`users.edit`; transactional owner-set lock, no self-delete, no last-owner delete; FK cascade drops accounts/sessions/tokens). Satisfies `L2-AUTH-38`, `L2-AUTH-39`, `L2-AUTH-42`, `L2-AUTH-36`. (User creation moved to the route handler above.)
- `apps/web/app/backflip/(protected)/settings/page.tsx` + `_actions.ts` — guarded by capability `settings` (owner) at route + action level.

clauses.title: Authorization (RBAC)
clauses.body:
- One capability map in `permissions.ts` drives everything: nav visibility, edit-button rendering, route guards, and action checks. Add a nav item → give it a `capability`; add a page → guard with `requireCapability`.
- Grants: owner = all; admin = dashboard + account + users.view (read-only users, no settings); teammate = dashboard + account only. See `L2-AUTH-21`.
- Server-side is authoritative (`L2-AUTH-22`): hiding UI is cosmetic; `requireCapability` (pages) + `can*` checks (actions) do the enforcing. The edge `proxy` still gates the whole `/backflip/*` subtree for authentication; capability checks are per-route inside it.

clauses.title: Account page (`/backflip/account`) — self-service (built)
clauses.body:
- `account/page.tsx` — server, `requireCapability("account")` (all roles). Cards: **Profile** (name + verified email change), **Password**, **Login methods** (read-only). `passwordHash` read only to derive a boolean; never sent to client.
- `account/_components/profile-section.tsx` — name, `useActionState(saveProfile)`, summary ↔ inline form.
- `account/_components/email-section.tsx` (`AccountEmailSection`) — request email change via `requestEmailChange`; keeps the pending "verification sent" message visible (address not yet changed).
- `account/_components/password-section.tsx` — change/set password via `changePassword`; toast on success.
- `account/_actions.ts` (self-scoped — always `session.user.id`, never a client id):
  - `saveProfile` — update name.
  - `changePassword` — verify current bcrypt when a hash exists (OAuth-only users may set a first password), min-8 + confirm, then `sendPasswordChangedEmail`; bumps `tokenVersion` (invalidates all sessions incl. own).
  - `requestEmailChange` — **step-up** (re-verify current password when a hash exists) + per-account rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT`) → validate + availability → mint `email_change` token (`newEmail`) → `sendEmailChangeVerification` to the NEW address. Requires configured email (else "configure email first"). Does NOT change the address.
  - `confirmEmailChange(token)` — consume token **passing `userId`** (a token owned by another account is rejected without being consumed → can't burn a victim's pending change), re-check availability, swap `email` + bump `tokenVersion`, `sendEmailChangedNotice` to the OLD address.
- `account/verify-email/page.tsx` + `_components/verify-email-confirm.tsx` — target of the verify link (protected). Button (not auto-run, avoids prefetch consuming the token) calls `confirmEmailChange`. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-27`.

clauses.title: Password recovery (`(auth)`, public)
clauses.body:
- `(auth)/_actions.ts` (both short-circuit with "Password sign-in is disabled" when `!isCredentialsEnabled()`):
  - `requestPasswordReset` — if the email exists AND under the per-account rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT`), mint a `password_reset` token + `sendPasswordResetEmail`; ALWAYS returns a generic success (no user enumeration — over-limit silently skips). Satisfies `L2-AUTH-28`, `L2-AUTH-37`.
  - `resetPassword` — validate token (min-8 + confirm), set `passwordHash` + bump `tokenVersion`, `sendPasswordChangedEmail`. Satisfies `L2-AUTH-28`, `L2-AUTH-36`.
- `(auth)/forgot-password/page.tsx` + form — public request page.
- `(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx` + form — public set-new-password page (token from query).
- `proxy.ts` — `RECOVERY_PATHS` (`/backflip/forgot-password`, `/backflip/reset-password`) bypass the auth gate (public). Satisfies `L2-AUTH-01`.
- `login/_components/login-form.tsx` — "Forgot password?" link next to the password field.

Satisfies `L2-AUTH-29`, `L2-AUTH-37`.

clauses.title: Implementation notes
clauses.body:
- **Credentials → JWT**: Credentials provider forces `jwt` session strategy; adapter still used to persist Google accounts.
- **Google pre-registration**: `signIn` callback returns false unless `db` has a `user` with that email → no OAuth self-signup. `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true` links Google to the seeded user by email (emails pre-registered/trusted). The seeded owner is pre-registered, so Google sign-in works for them by default — including when `ADMIN_PASSWORD` was omitted (Google-only owner, see [[db]] `init-owner`).
- **Google-only mode**: `AUTH_CREDENTIALS_ENABLED=false` drops the Credentials provider and the password form (and blocks the recovery actions). Fail-safe: honored only when Google is configured, so credentials stay on otherwise — a deployment can't be left with no sign-in method (`L2-AUTH-33`).
- **Session revocation (`tokenVersion`)**: JWTs are stateless, so forced logout works via a version counter on `user`. The `jwt` callback re-reads it per authenticated request (one indexed lookup — the accepted cost of revocation) and flags stale tokens; `session` then yields no `user`. Bumped on password change / reset / confirmed email change → ALL sessions invalidate, **including the actor's own** (self-service password change logs you out too — intended). The edge proxy only sees token *presence*, so revoked-but-present cookies pass the edge but are caught node-side by `requireCapability`; the login page's `auth()` redirect is likewise validity-aware (prevents a login↔home loop). Unverified end-to-end here (no DB/auth server in-session) — typecheck + build only.
- **Recovery rate limiting is per-account, not per-IP** (`countRecentTokens` over `user_token.createdAt`). It caps repeated reset/change emails to a known account but doesn't stop distributed enumeration by IP — a future edge/middleware limiter would.
- **Login throttle (`L2-AUTH-40`)**: separate from recovery limiting. `authorize` blocks after `LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10) failed attempts per `IP:email` within `LOGIN_WINDOW_MS` (15 min); a blocked attempt returns the same generic `null` as a bad password (no lockout signal → no enumeration). Only failures count; a success resets the key. In-process (`rate-limit.ts`) so it holds per Node process — the deployment runs one pm2 process/container bound to loopback, so that's the whole surface; a horizontally-scaled deployment would need a shared store. Client IP comes from `x-forwarded-for`/`x-real-ip` (the proxy sets these; `L2-DEVOPS-05` nginx/Caddy forward them).
- **Google `email_verified` (`L2-AUTH-41`)**: `signIn` rejects a Google login whose `profile.email_verified !== true` BEFORE the pre-registration lookup. Because `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking` links by email, this stops an identity asserting an unverified address from linking into a pre-registered user.
- **Env loading**: Next runs in `apps/web`, so it won't read root `.env*` on its own. `dev` script uses `dotenv -e ../../.env -e ../../.env.local` to inject root env (needed by edge proxy + node route). Docker app gets env via compose `env_file`.
- **Edge/node split**: proxy stays edge-safe (`getToken`, no db). Full auth (adapter + bcrypt + pg) is node-only, used by the route handler.
- `packages/typescript-config/nextjs.json` sets `declaration:false` — fixes next-auth v5 TS2742 ("inferred type cannot be named") under `noEmit`.

clauses.title: Unit tests (vitest, `corepack yarn workspace web test`)
clauses.body:
Colocated next to the sources they protect. They exist to freeze the security invariants, not for coverage.
- `app/_lib/auth/permissions.test.ts` — capability matrix per role (`L2-AUTH-21`).
- `app/_lib/auth/config.test.ts` — auth-mode flags via `vi.stubEnv`: both Google vars required; `AUTH_CREDENTIALS_ENABLED=false` honored only with Google configured; a sweep asserts ≥1 sign-in method always remains (`L2-AUTH-33/34`).
- `app/_lib/auth/auth-callbacks.test.ts` — the real Auth.js config object, captured by mocking `next-auth`'s default export (`NextAuth(config)`), with `@workspace/db` swapped for a stub `db.query.users.findFirst` and `@auth/drizzle-adapter` stubbed out. Covers provider composition per auth mode (`L2-AUTH-05/33/34`), `signIn` Google pre-registration incl. profile-email fallback, credentials pass-through, and the `email_verified` gate (verified+registered → allow; unverified → deny before lookup) (`L2-AUTH-10/11/14/41`), credentials `authorize` with a real bcrypt hash — wrong password / plaintext hash / no hash / unknown email / blank input all → `null` (`L2-AUTH-09`), and the revocation path: `jwt` stamps then revalidates `tokenVersion` (mismatch or missing user → `invalid`), `session` drops `user` (`L2-AUTH-36`). Note: `Credentials()` keeps the user-supplied `authorize` under `provider.options` until Auth.js init merges it — the test reads it there.
- `app/_lib/rate-limit.test.ts` — fixed-window limiter via an injectable clock: blocks only at the cap, resets after the window, `reset()` clears immediately, keys are independent, `retryAfterMs` reports remaining time (`L2-AUTH-40`, `L2-AI-22`).
- `app/_lib/auth/tokens.test.ts` — recording stub for the Drizzle query builder (`insert/update/select` chains), real `generateToken`/`hashToken` via `importActual`. Locks: invalidate-then-insert order, 60-min TTL, hash-only storage (raw token absent from the insert), lookup by hash not raw, single-use consume + rejection of wrong-type/consumed/expired/empty, the `userId` ownership guard (wrong owner → null, not consumed; matching owner → consumed), `RATE_LIMIT = {3, 15min}` and the count cutoff (`L2-AUTH-29/31/37`).
- Not unit-testable without a real DB (left to e2e): actual SQL semantics of the invalidation/rate-limit `WHERE` clauses, `user_token` uniqueness, and adapter account linking.

clauses.title: Role rename (migration 0002)
clauses.body: - `user_role` value `member` → `teammate`. drizzle-kit generated a drop/recreate (`SET DATA TYPE text` → `DROP TYPE` → recreate → recast); hand-replaced with `ALTER TYPE ... RENAME VALUE 'member' TO 'teammate'` + `ALTER COLUMN role SET DEFAULT 'teammate'`. Rename preserves rows + the default binding and reaches the same end state as the `0002` snapshot (drop/recreate would reject any existing `member` row on the recast). Not yet applied here (no DB in the web session); apply with `db:migrate` when a DB is up.

clauses.title: Gotcha — type-change migrations
clauses.body: - `drizzle-kit generate` emits column type changes as bare `SET DATA TYPE` with no `USING` cast. For incompatible casts (e.g. text→integer) Postgres rejects the SQL, and `drizzle-kit migrate` fails *quietly* (prints "applying…", no success line, journal not advanced — looks like a no-op). Fix: hand-edit the generated SQL to add `USING <col>::<type>`, or `db:push` in dev. (This is what broke the old `0001`; the baseline was squashed to avoid it.)
